q: The scalar product of vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ is defined as $\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B} = AB \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$. This product is also called the _____
e: A · B = AB cos θ. That number is the dot product, also called the scalar product. The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as A · B = AB cos θ, where θ is the angle between A and B. This product is also called the dot product. Cross product or vector product is not this quantity.

q: The vector product of vectors $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ is denoted by $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}$. This product is also called the _____
e: A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B. The vector product of vectors A and B is denoted by A × B. This product is also called the cross product. Do not trade cross product for scalar product or dot product.

q: The scalar product has the commutative property described by the equation _____
e: Dot products make scalars with cos θ. Cross products make perpendicular vectors with sin θ. The scalar product has the commutative property described by the equation A · B = B · A. A × B = B × A or A · B = -B · A is a different relation from A · B = B · A.

q: The vector product does not obey the commutative property, and instead follows the relation _____
e: The cross product anticommutes: A × B = −(B × A). Swap the order and the vector flips. The vector product does not obey the commutative property, and instead follows the relation A × B = - (B × A). A × B = B × A or A · B = - (B · A) is a different relation from A × B = - (B × A).

q: Work is a scalar quantity because it is the _____ of force and displacement.
e: Work is F · s, a dot product, so work is a scalar. Work is a scalar quantity because it is the scalar product of force and displacement. Do not trade scalar product for vector product or cross product.

q: The direction of the vector product $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}$ is determined by using the _____
e: Dot products make scalars with cos θ. Cross products make perpendicular vectors with sin θ. The direction of the vector product A × B is determined by using the right-hand rule. Do not trade right-hand rule for left-hand rule or Fleming’s rule.

q: The result of the scalar product of two vectors is a _____
e: A dot product is a scalar. The result of the scalar product of two vectors is a scalar. Vector or tensor is not this quantity.

q: The result of the vector product of two vectors is a _____
e: A cross product is a vector. The result of the vector product of two vectors is a vector. Do not trade vector for scalar or unitless number.

q: In circular motion, tangential velocity is expressed in terms of radius $\mathbf{r}$ and angular velocity $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ as _____
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. In circular motion, tangential velocity is expressed in terms of radius r and angular velocity boldsymbol{ω} as v = boldsymbol{ω} × r. v = boldsymbol{ω} · r or v = r · boldsymbol{ω} is a different relation from v = boldsymbol{ω} × r.

q: The magnitude of the vector product $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}$ is given by _____
e: The size of A × B is AB sin θ. The magnitude of the vector product A × B is given by AB sin θ. AB cos θ or AB tan θ is a different relation from AB sin θ.

q: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the _____
e: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the torque. Do not trade torque for moment of inertia or angular momentum.

q: Torque is a _____ quantity.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. Torque is a vector quantity. Do not trade vector for scalar or dimensionless.

q: The vector form of torque is expressed as _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The vector form of torque is expressed as boldsymbol{tau} = F × r. boldsymbol{tau} = F · r or boldsymbol{tau} = r · F is a different relation from boldsymbol{tau} = F × r.

q: The magnitude of torque is defined as the product of the force and the _____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The magnitude of torque is defined as the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum. Do not trade perpendicular distance for horizontal distance or angular distance.

q: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum is also called the _____
e: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum is also called the moment arm. Do not trade moment arm for lever arm or force arm.

q: In SI units, torque is measured in _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. In SI units, torque is measured in newton metre (N m). joule or kg m² s⁻² is a different relation from newton metre (N m).

q: If a force acts at an angle of $90^{\circ}$ to the lever arm, then the moment arm $d$ is equal to _____
e: If a force acts at an angle of 90° to the lever arm, then the moment arm d is equal to r. zero or r sin θ is a different relation from r.

q: The line along which a force is considered to act is called the _____
a: line of action of the force
e: The line along which a force is considered to act is called the line of action of the force. Axis of rotation or pivot line is not this quantity.

q: Examples of the turning effect of force include all of the following EXCEPT _____
a: tightening a nut with a spanner
e: Examples of the turning effect of force include all of the following EXCEPT dropping a ball vertically. Opening a door or tightening a nut with a spanner is not this quantity.

q: The point about which an object turns when a force is applied is known as the _____
e: The point about which an object turns when a force is applied is known as the fulcrum or pivot. Do not trade fulcrum or pivot for center of mass or axis of symmetry.

q: The moment of inertia of a particle of mass $m$ at distance $r$ from the axis of rotation is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of a particle of mass m at distance r from the axis of rotation is mr². mr or m/r² is a different relation from mr².

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle and the _____ of its distance from the axis.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle and the square of its distance from the axis. Do not trade square for cube or first power.

q: The SI unit of moment of inertia is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The SI unit of moment of inertia is kg m². kg m or N m is a different relation from kg m².

q: Moment of inertia must be specified with respect to a chosen _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. Moment of inertia must be specified with respect to a chosen axis of rotation. Center of mass or pivot point is not this quantity.

q: For a solid sphere rotating about its axis, the moment of inertia is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. For a solid sphere rotating about its axis, the moment of inertia is (2)/(5) MR². (1)/(2) MR² or MR² is a different relation from (2)/(5) MR².

q: For a hoop or cylindrical shell rotating about its central axis, the moment of inertia is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. For a hoop or cylindrical shell rotating about its central axis, the moment of inertia is MR². (1)/(2) MR² or (1)/(12) ML² is a different relation from MR².

q: For a long thin rod rotating about an axis through its center and perpendicular to its length, the moment of inertia is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. For a long thin rod rotating about an axis through its center and perpendicular to its length, the moment of inertia is (1)/(12) ML². (1)/(3) ML² or ML² is a different relation from (1)/(12) ML².

q: For a long thin rod rotating about an axis through one end and perpendicular to its length, the moment of inertia is _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. For a long thin rod rotating about an axis through one end and perpendicular to its length, the moment of inertia is (1)/(3) ML². (1)/(12) ML² or (1)/(2) ML² is a different relation from (1)/(3) ML².

q: The relationship between torque $\tau$, moment of inertia $I$, and angular acceleration $\alpha$ is _____
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. The relationship between torque tau, moment of inertia I, and angular acceleration α is tau = I α. tau = I / α or tau = α / I is a different relation from tau = I α.

q: The center of gravity of an object of regular shape and uniform density is located at its _____
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. The center of gravity of an object of regular shape and uniform density is located at its geometrical center. Do not trade geometrical center for bottom edge or top surface.

q: When a system is in static equilibrium, the resultant force on the system is _____
e: When a system is in static equilibrium, the resultant force on the system is zero. Do not trade zero for maximum or equal to weight.

q: When a system is in static equilibrium, the resultant torque on the system is _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. When a system is in static equilibrium, the resultant torque on the system is zero. Maximum or equal to angular momentum is not this quantity.

q: The principle of moments states that for a pivoted object to be in balance, the total clockwise moment must equal the total _____ moment.
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. The principle of moments states that for a pivoted object to be in balance, the total clockwise moment must equal the total anticlockwise moment. Downward or horizontal is not this quantity.

q: Applications of the principle of moments include all of the following EXCEPT _____
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. Applications of the principle of moments include all of the following EXCEPT free-falling object. Beam balance or building site crane is not this quantity.

q: In static equilibrium under parallel forces, the sum of upward forces equals the sum of _____ forces.
e: In static equilibrium under parallel forces, the sum of upward forces equals the sum of downward forces. Sideways or torque is not this quantity.

q: For a uniform metre rule balanced horizontally, its weight is considered to act at the _____ mark.
e: For a uniform metre rule balanced horizontally, its weight is considered to act at the 50 cm mark. Do not trade 50 cm for 0 cm or 100 cm.

q: The conditions of static equilibrium require both force balance and _____ balance.
e: The conditions of static equilibrium require both force balance and torque balance. Energy or velocity is not this quantity.

q: If an object is uniform and symmetric, its center of gravity lies at its _____
e: If an object is uniform and symmetric, its center of gravity lies at its geometrical center. Edge or fulcrum is not this quantity.

q: In analyzing equilibrium of extended bodies, we often take moments about the _____ to simplify calculations.
e: In analyzing equilibrium of extended bodies, we often take moments about the pivot to simplify calculations. Center of mass or top end is not this quantity.

q: The reaction force at a support in equilibrium problems is typically _____
e: The reaction force at a support in equilibrium problems is typically part of force balance. Do not trade part of force balance for ignored or equal to applied torque.

q: Angular momentum $L$ is defined as the product of moment of inertia $I$ and _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. Angular momentum L is defined as the product of moment of inertia I and angular velocity. Do not trade angular velocity for angular acceleration or torque.

q: The SI unit of angular momentum is _____
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. The SI unit of angular momentum is kg m² s⁻¹. N m or kg m s⁻¹ is a different relation from kg m² s⁻¹.

q: Angular momentum is a _____ quantity.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. Angular momentum is a vector quantity. Do not trade vector for scalar or dimensionless.

q: The law of conservation of angular momentum states that if there is no net external torque, the total angular momentum of the system is _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The law of conservation of angular momentum states that if there is no net external torque, the total angular momentum of the system is constant. Do not trade constant for zero or increasing.

q: An ice skater spinning with arms extended pulls her arms inward. Her moment of inertia decreases, so her angular speed _____
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. An ice skater spinning with arms extended pulls her arms inward. Her moment of inertia decreases, so her angular speed increases.

q: When a springboard diver rotates after jumping off the board, continued rotation occurs because _____
e: When a springboard diver rotates after jumping off the board, continued rotation occurs because angular momentum is conserved. Gravity provides torque or muscles keep working is not this quantity.

q: If the moment of inertia of a rotating object increases by a factor of 2 with no external torque, its angular speed becomes _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. If the moment of inertia of a rotating object increases by a factor of 2 with no external torque, its angular speed becomes half. Twice or unchanged is not this quantity.

q: The direction of angular momentum is the same as the direction of _____
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. The direction of angular momentum is the same as the direction of angular velocity. Linear velocity or centripetal force is not this quantity.

q: In symbols, the condition for conservation of angular momentum is _____
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. In symbols, the condition for conservation of angular momentum is sum tau = 0 Rightarrow L = constant. sum F = 0 Rightarrow L = constant or sum tau ≠ 0 Rightarrow L = constant is a different relation from sum tau = 0 Rightarrow L = constant.

q: To slow down her rotation, an ice skater should _____
e: To slow down her rotation, an ice skater should stretch arms outward. Do not trade stretch arms outward for pull arms inward or bend forward.
